title: The Messengership Of Prophet Muhammad 16th Degree 3rd Proof The Uniqueness Of Sharia Islam Worship And Supplication

questions.question: What does this part say the Prophet brought to people?
questions.answer: A special way of life, worship, calling people to truth, and faith.

questions.question: How long does the passage say his law guided a large part of people?
questions.answer: For fourteen centuries.

questions.question: About how many people does the passage say were guided by Islam in each century?
questions.answer: About three hundred million people.

questions.question: How did Islam help people’s minds and hearts?
questions.answer: It taught their minds and gave light and purity to their hearts.

questions.question: How did Islam help people’s souls and spirits?
questions.answer: It trained their souls and helped their spirits grow.

questions.question: What made the Prophet stand out in worship?
questions.answer: He was the first and best in doing the worship of his religion.

questions.question: What two feelings are named with his worship?
questions.answer: Piety and fear of Allah.

questions.question: Did he worship only when life was easy, or also during hard work and struggle?
questions.answer: Also during hard work and struggle.

questions.question: Did he copy someone else in worship?
questions.answer: No, he did not copy anyone.

questions.question: What prayer book is named in this passage?
questions.answer: Jawshan al-Kabir.

questions.question: What did he do in that prayer?
questions.answer: He described his Lord with great knowledge.

questions.question: How does the passage compare later saints and knowers to him in this kind of prayer?
questions.answer: It says they could not reach his level, even together.

questions.question: What main idea does the whole passage teach about him?
questions.answer: He had no equal in religion, worship, and prayer.

questions.question: Who is this passage mostly about?
questions.answer: Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the law that came with him?
questions.answer: It has no equal.

questions.question: Why does the passage say this law is special?
questions.answer: It ruled justly and carefully over many people for a very long time.

questions.question: What does the passage say came from his actions, words, and inner state?
questions.answer: Islam.

questions.question: What jobs did Islam do for people in each century?
questions.answer: It guided them, protected them, taught them, and helped clean their hearts.

questions.question: What other good changes did Islam bring to people inside themselves?
questions.answer: It improved their souls and helped their spirits move forward.

questions.question: In worship, what kind of example was the Prophet?
questions.answer: He was the best example and the first to practice it fully.

questions.question: How carefully did he do worship?
questions.answer: With full care and deep understanding.

questions.question: What does the passage show by saying he worshiped even during struggle?
questions.answer: That he stayed devoted to Allah in all times.

questions.question: What is one reason the passage gives that he is unmatched in prayer?
questions.answer: His knowledge of Allah in his prayers was greater than others could reach.

questions.question: What does the passage say people would think after reading part of the Jawshan’s meaning?
questions.answer: They would say it has no equal too.

questions.question: Which is stronger in the passage: saying he was good, or saying he was unmatched?
questions.answer: It says he was unmatched.

questions.question: What is the big lesson from this passage?
questions.answer: The Prophet was unique in what he brought and in how he worshiped Allah.

questions.question: What are some of the things the Prophet brought, according to this passage?
questions.answer: A law, Islam, worship, a call, and faith.

questions.question: Does the passage say something else like them could be found?
questions.answer: No, it says nothing like them exists.

questions.question: What part of humanity does the passage say his law managed?
questions.answer: One fifth of humanity.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the way that law was carried out?
questions.answer: In a fair and careful way.

questions.question: From what does the passage say Islam came forth?
questions.answer: From his deeds, words, and inner life.

questions.question: Name one way Islam helped people besides teaching them.
questions.answer: It gave them safety and support, or it cleaned their hearts, or it trained their souls.

questions.question: What does “unlettered” mean here?
questions.answer: He did not learn by ordinary reading and writing like others.

questions.question: Even though he was busy and struggling, what did he still do?
questions.answer: He still completed worship very carefully.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the beginning and end of his worship?
questions.answer: He joined them in a complete and perfect way.

questions.question: What special prayer is named from his many prayers?
questions.answer: Jawshan al-Kabir.

questions.question: In that prayer, what did he show about his Sustainer?
questions.answer: Very great knowledge and beautiful understanding.

questions.question: Could later holy people reach the same level in describing Allah?
questions.answer: No, they could not.

questions.question: If someone reads part of the explanation of the Jawshan, what conclusion does the passage say they may reach?
questions.answer: That it too is without equal.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the religion the Prophet brought?
questions.answer: It teaches that it is perfect and has no match.

questions.question: Why is the law he brought called special in this passage?
questions.answer: Because it served many people for centuries with justice.

questions.question: What does the passage say Islam was for people’s minds?
questions.answer: A teacher.

questions.question: What does the passage say Islam was for people’s hearts?
questions.answer: A light and a way to become clean.

questions.question: What does the passage say Islam was for people’s souls?
questions.answer: A way to grow and be trained.

questions.question: What does the passage say Islam was for people’s spirits?
questions.answer: A source of progress.

questions.question: How was the Prophet different from others in worship?
questions.answer: He led everyone in doing it and did it most completely.

questions.question: What was he careful to keep, even in difficult times?
questions.answer: The duties of worship.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by saying he worshiped without imitation?
questions.answer: He was not just copying another person.

questions.question: What is one thing the Jawshan al-Kabir shows about him?
questions.answer: His prayers had very deep knowledge of Allah.

questions.question: Who could not match his level of knowledge in prayer?
questions.answer: The gnostics and saints who came after him.

questions.question: According to this passage, did the Prophet bring only rules, or also faith and worship?
questions.answer: He brought rules, faith, worship, and a call to truth.

questions.question: What does the passage say about finding something better than what he brought?
questions.answer: It says nothing better exists.

questions.question: How many centuries does the passage mention when talking about his law?
questions.answer: Fourteen centuries.

questions.question: How many people in each century does the passage mention when talking about Islam’s guidance?
questions.answer: Three hundred million men.

questions.question: Give two ways Islam helped people in the passage.
questions.answer: It taught their minds and cleaned their hearts.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the Prophet’s place in worship?
questions.answer: He was first and foremost.

questions.question: What does the passage connect with his worship besides piety?
questions.answer: Fear of Allah.

questions.question: What does it show that he worshiped during struggle and busyness?
questions.answer: That his worship stayed strong all the time.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the fullness of his worship?
questions.answer: He carried it out completely and deeply.

questions.question: What is the name of the prayer mentioned as one among many?
questions.answer: Jawshan al-Kabir.

questions.question: What was special about the way he spoke of Allah in that prayer?
questions.answer: It showed a very high level of knowing Allah.

questions.question: What happened when later great worshipers tried to reach that same level?
questions.answer: They still could not equal it.

questions.question: What big claim does this passage make about the Prophet’s law and religion?
questions.answer: That they are unlike anything else and have no equal.

questions.question: What shows the strength of that law over time?
questions.answer: It guided a large part of humanity for fourteen centuries.

questions.question: What two words describe how that law was carried out?
questions.answer: Justly and precisely.

questions.question: Where does the passage say Islam came from in the Prophet’s life?
questions.answer: From what he did, said, and felt inside.

questions.question: Was Islam only for teaching facts, or did it help the whole person?
questions.answer: It helped the whole person.

questions.question: What parts of the person did Islam help, according to the passage?
questions.answer: The mind, heart, soul, and spirit.

questions.question: In worship, what kind of leader was the Prophet?
questions.answer: The leading example for everyone.

questions.question: What does the passage say about his worship when life was busy and hard?
questions.answer: He still kept worship with full care.

questions.question: What does the passage say about learning worship from others in his case?
questions.answer: He did not do it by copying others.

questions.question: Which prayer is given as a strong example of his excellence in supplication?
questions.answer: Jawshan al-Kabir.

questions.question: What does the passage say this prayer shows about his knowledge of Allah?
questions.answer: It shows knowledge greater than others reached.

questions.question: What do people understand after looking at part of the explanation of that prayer?
questions.answer: That this prayer is also unmatched.
